meaningMnemonic: Set fire to a geoduck if you want to annoy it. Fire won't kill a geoduck, but have you ever been on fire? It's not really pleasant. So you'll just annoy it pretty badly. Hints Imagine how annoyed you would be if someone set YOU on fire for no reason. The geoduck has every reason to find you annoying, dude.
readingMnemonic: You know who loves annoying geoducks more than anyone else in the universe? Han ( はん ) Solo! If you watch Star Wars closely enough you can see him shooting geoducks with his blaster and catching them on fire for fun. Hints Think how annoying it must be to be a geoduck when Han Solo comes around.

meaningMnemonic: "For the samurai , it is a jackhammer that they will lack ." That is the latest article of the law written about samurai, hundreds of years after katana were taken away. This article was written with great sincerity by the government. Hints By writing up new articles and laws they keep taking things away from samurai. First the katana, now jackhammers?
readingMnemonic: The one who wrote these article s with such sincerity was Genghis Khan ( かん ). Hints Genghis Khan knew that samurai were a threat to his kingdom, so he took away their secondary weapon, the jackhammer.

meaningMnemonic: If, again and again, you behave like an insect , you might as well be a barbarian . Hints Again and again, these insect-like barbarians are harassing you and your lands. What shall we do, m'lord?
readingMnemonic: " BAN ( ばん ) the barbarians! Ban them, I say!," you loudly declare as the lord of these lands. Hints Picture yourself as the lord of your lands, screaming "BAN them" at the top of your lungs. You'll finally expel these insect-like barbarians that have been plaguing your lands again and again.

meaningMnemonic: Under this canopy is the Mona Lisa , being sold for cheap, what a great bargain ! Hints Look really closely at this Mona Lisa. Hmm, I don't remember her having a mustache, but I guess it is a little dark under this canopy.
readingMnemonic: This Mona Lisa is such a bargain because it's just a ren tal ( れん )! Hints No wonder this moustached Mona Lisa is such a bargain. You can really get anything as a rental these days, huh?

meaningMnemonic: If you want to slice the power out of someone just censure them. Then they'll be cut down in front of everyone and they'll feel super embarrassed. It's the best way to slice them down without actually cutting them and getting arrested. Hints Picture yourself as you slice the power out of that senator you hate by censuring them in front of the world!
readingMnemonic: Once you censure them and they lose all their power, they'll be just another guy ( がい ). A normal guy with everything lost to him. HAHAHA! Hints Look at that guy now. What a loser.

meaningMnemonic: If you think a tree looks sweet you have to be certain before you bite into it. Trees are really hard, and usually pretty bitter (believe me) so if you don't want a mouthful of broken teeth, sap, and sadness, you really need to be sure it's the one before you start munching. Hints Which tree do you think is sweet? That one? Or that one? Are you absolutely certain? I hope you are!
readingMnemonic: If you really want to be certain , and not just guess, take out your bow ling ( ぼう ) ball and roll it as hard as you can into the tree. If its the right one it will let out a sweet smell, if it's not the tree will punch you. Hints So now let me ask you again, are you certain, or would you like to try the bowling ball test?

meaningMnemonic: An arrow is shot from heaven and hits right between your mouth and your mustache to correct your crooked smile. It also straighten s your teeth and the crooked cut of your mustache too. Who told you that looked good? Well, it doesn't matter. The heaven arrow corrected it for you. Hints An arrow from heaven will correct all your problems!
readingMnemonic: These heavenly correct ing arrows actually come from きょう と . They hate seeing people with crooked mustaches, so they shoot them out on the regular. It just looks like they're coming from heaven because they fall out of the sky. Hints If you want someone to correct your teeth or mustache, just wander around きょうと , staring up at the sky. Then when you see an arrow, run for it and try to catch it with your face!

meaningMnemonic: You ate some grain s that made you so sick it feels like a knife is stabbing in your guts and all your poop is falling out. This is called diarrhea . Everyone's had diarrhea before, so you should know this feeling by now. Hints Imagine back to the last time you ate something bad and it gave you diarrhea. It felt like someone was sticking you with a knife, didn't it?
readingMnemonic: The diarrhea is here. It's happening. And it smells so awful you can't breathe. You have to take some hollow reed s ( り ) and shove them up your nose and out the bathroom door so you can get some fresh air in you. Hints You learned this reed technique from a group of ninjas who use them to breathe underwater, and you never thought you'd use them like this.

meaningMnemonic: If you ride a scooter with your fingers around an axe you're going to die . I mean, probably. There's a 99% chance you'll die. Hints Picture someone else riding a scooter with an axe in their fingertips. That's so dangerous! One bump, one bad turn, and that axe slips and they'll die.
readingMnemonic: You slip. The axe collides with your face. You die . But... wait! There's a bright, blue glow and suddenly you're un-dead. You watch in slow motion as your holy blue sa ber ( せい ) brings you back to life and takes the hit from the axe instead. Wait, no! It shatters. Hints Your holy blue saber died for you. It saved you from certain death and now it died. After all you've been through together. All 60 levels. This is the end.

meaningMnemonic: You're stuck in your car during a tsunami and all you have to break out is an axe . You whack and whack but you're only gradually making progress. You thought an axe would be an easy way to get out of a car but it's not working like you'd planned! You have to make more than gradual progress if you don't want to drown. Hints Imagine gradually denting your car door open with an axe while you're trapped in a tsunami. This isn't fast enough!
readingMnemonic: As you're gradually making your door open with the axe you look up to see the New York Yankees floating by on top of their bus. You yell, " YO YA NKEES ( ようや ) to get their attention. They see your gradual progress and start throwing balls at your car to help dent it open. Hints YO YANKEES! Gradually yelling that saved your life!

meaningMnemonic: You see twenty slide s lined up like a grid . You don't know who put them here, but they almost look like the grid paper you do your maths homework in. But who would use a slide as grid paper? Hints Picture twenty slides laid out in a grid system.
readingMnemonic: As you stare at the slide grid you see some people come out and overhear them talk about their mass maths ( ます ) tournament happening later today. Oohhh it IS a giant grid. And they're going to use it to do maths later! Hints You can make a grid out of anything if you set your mind to it. And you can do math anywhere as long as you have some grid paper!

meaningMnemonic: Have you heard the tale of the woman who fell in love with a coat rack during a full moon and made him her groom ? It's a true story! She even had a wedding ceremony and had more coat racks sitting in the groom's side. The moon will make people do craaaazy things. Hints Imagine what it would be like to fall in love with a coat rack and make it YOUR groom.
readingMnemonic: Since their wedding happened under the full moon, the groom wore his special moon coa t ( むこ ) to the ceremony. This is the ideal coat for a groom to wear, since they can keep wearing it all through their honeymoon. Hints Try to imagine what this moon coat looks like. Does it glow in the dark like the moon shines at night? Or does it instead have a rugged texture like the moon's surface? Or maybe both?

meaningMnemonic: This cage is full of flowers on the right side to hide the fact that you're in here too. Hints You don't really want to be in this cage, but there were some things you didn't want to do today, so you hid. Luckily these flowers block the right side of the cage and hide you completely.
readingMnemonic: As you hide the ghost of Toku gawa ( とく ) Ieyasu appears before you, inside the cage! His arms are crossed and he's shaking his head at you. "Do you think I managed to become the first shougun of Japan by hiding?" Hints "N-no?" you respond. "Wrong! I hid all the time. There's nothing wrong with hiding, you're doing a great job." he says, and disappears.

meaningMnemonic: You say something to a boot when you want to be humble . You're down there because you're bowing in front of the person you're humbling yourself before. Because of that, your face is really close to their boots and you're speaking directly at them, instead of at the person's face, so it's more discreet . Hints Picture yourself trying to be humble. You're down on the ground talking to a pair of boots. You don't dare raise your eyes past that.
readingMnemonic: You're being humble like this because those boots belong to the Kin g ( きん ) of England. You can't just say whatever you want at eye level to a king. He'll have your head chopped off for insolence, or worse! Hints Imagine saying something to the King. Get low down on the ground to be as humble as you can. Whisper into the King's boots. Lick them if you have to.

meaningMnemonic: Flowers that you oversee are always indigo . You aren't sure why though... Hints Imagine if every flower you were supposed to oversee was indigo. Indigo everywhere!
readingMnemonic: Wait, maybe these flowers are only indigo because there is something wrong with your eye s ( あい )! Maybe your eyes are indigo and that's why it's all you see! Hints Can you imagine having indigo-only seeing eyes? I can. Because of this awesome mnemonic.

meaningMnemonic: You grab a tree to help you reach the bar out in the ocean, using it as a jetty leading straight to it. Now you can walk out on your makeshift pier and go get drinks without needing a boat or getting wet. Hints Imagine laying your tree into the water to make your own jetty extending out to the floating bar in the ocean. Innovative!
readingMnemonic: You also made this jetty so it would be easier for San ta-san ( さん ) to dock his sleigh. Oh, you didn't know? His sleigh is more of a speed boat now, and he wants a refreshing drink after delivering all those presents. You get extra presents for making him a jetty, so win-win. Hints Picture Santa-san coming in from the ocean on his speedboat and docking on your jetty so he can go relax in the bar. Imagine the mountain of presents he lays on the jetty for you as thanks.

meaningMnemonic: You set up a canopy over a patch of dirt because you're setting up a manor here — you know, a big rural estate , probably with serfs and stuff. Hints Not only will the canopy protect your manorial estate from the elements, it will also let would-be trespassers know that this is your private patch of dirt that they're not allowed to set foot on.
readingMnemonic: The establishment of your manor was approved by the sho gun ( しょう ) himself. The shogun presides over all the territory in the land, so you can't set up a private estate without his blessing. Hints You keep a big portrait of the shogun on the wall of your manor house to let all the serfs and peasants on your estate know who they'll have to deal with if they question your authority.

meaningMnemonic: Put a yakuza member in a prison on the sun and he'll become a martyr to all the other yakuza still on earth. He died up there so the rest of them wouldn't have to. Because they definitely aren't getting caught now, if the penalty is a burning death in the new sun prison. Hints Imagine all the yakuza coming out into the streets and holding up signs saying this guy was a martyr. A hero to all who do bad stuff in bad groups but don't wanna get caught.
readingMnemonic: The only reason he ended up a martyr in the first place is because they put him up there in June ( じゅん ). Everyone knows the sun is way too hot for humans in June. It's summer! Hints Really, it's not the fault of the people who put him there that he's become a martyr. It's the month of June. PUNISH JUNE! PUT JUNE IN THE SUN PRISON! (Is what I assume those yakuza are shouting.)

meaningMnemonic: In the dirt , you find a lid under the table . You lift it to reveal a deep pit . Why is there a hole under your table? Hints You pull away the lid and crawl inside. There is a ladder that takes you deep into the pit.
readingMnemonic: When you reach the bottom of the pit , you hear someone scuffling around and the sounds of chains. You light a match and inch closer to see what it is. In the darkness, you see こう いち , starved and chained in a pit under your table. Hints After you've nursed こういち back to health, he explains that he was put here by a clone こういち –the very same こういち who became emperor. He tells you he can think of around 61-70 different pain levels of revenge, but also that "it probably wouldn't be worth it, so let's just hang out for a while instead. Ooh, are those cookies?"

meaningMnemonic: You're in a net but you have the ability to quit playing along and leave at any time. Hints Your captors think they have you trapped, but you know you can leave whenever you feel like it.
readingMnemonic: You don't know if you want to quit this charade until you feel an uncomfortable hea t ( ひ ). You look down and the net you're in is being hung above a large fire. Hints As the heat spreads you decide to leave. You hop out of the net and watch the shock spread in your captors eyes.

meaningMnemonic: If the death of a woman occurs it's because she was being reckless . People don't just die out of nowhere! They have to have done something super crazy to cause it. Right? Yes... right. Hints Picture yourself watching the news about a woman's death. The word RECKLESS?! pops up on your screen and keeps flashing. Huh, she must have been, you think to yourself.
readingMnemonic: As you watch the news about this reckless woman you find out that she died from mow ing ( もう ) her lawn. You're not sure how, but now you really believe that she had to be doing it really recklessly to die doing it. Hints Imagine what reckless thing that woman had to have done to die while mowing the lawn. Eww.

meaningMnemonic: As the tsunami hits your scooter and your car , it alters the wave, creating ripples . Hints They're hard to see because a tsunami is pretty big, but your scooter and car do create ripples in the water as it goes past.
readingMnemonic: Ripples come off of your scooter and car from when they were hit by a tsunami. More importantly, those things were ren tals ( れん ), so ripples or not, it doesn't matter if they were hit by a tsunami. Hints As you watch the ripples come off your car and scooter, be sure to imagine the relief you'd feel if you knew they were rentals and not something owned by you.

meaningMnemonic: The flowers that wash up on shore in tsunami s that we make into syrup is seaweed . Okay, so it's more like soup or tea than syrup, but you can make them both out of seaweed. Hints Seaweed is the flower of the sea!
readingMnemonic: Seaweed is true sou l ( そう ) food. Which means it's good for your soul. Didn't you ever read those books about chicken soup being good for your soul? Well that was a lie. Miso soup with seaweed is what's really good for your soul. Hints Feed your soul with seaweed and it will thank you. Promise! <3

meaningMnemonic: Tsunami 's have a certain tendency to secrete things as they go back out to sea. When they bash themselves onto the land they just throw a bunch of sea water around, but there are only certain things that they'll secrete when they're leaving. Hints Certain tsunami secretions are dangerous. Can you think of any?
readingMnemonic: Most tsunami's secrete he at ( ひ ). It takes a lot of energy for a tsunami to crash onto the land so the water is really really hot, and it has to secrete that heat as it's going back out to sea. Hints The next time someone asks you what does a tsunami secrete? You'll say heat!

meaningMnemonic: Use your mouth to sing and a shellfish to stroke your shamisen, and you'll be performing a shamisen song just like that! Yes, it's that easy. Just go find a shell, open your mouth, and you'll be singing one too in no time! Hints Imagine using your mouth to sing and a shell to play the shamisen to perform your shamisen song!
readingMnemonic: A shamisen song is just an 歌 ( うた ) but with a shamisen. They're still songs so they're said the exact same way! Hints A shamisen song is a song, yay!

meaningMnemonic: Half of a rice paddy is always on the shore . Japan is surrounded by water, after all. So it only makes sense that half of every rice paddy is right next to the ocean shore, right? Hints Picture a rice paddy. Half of it is trailing off into the shore. Hear the seagulls. Feel the ocean breeze!
readingMnemonic: You decide to walk along this shore when you see Han ( はん ) Solo lounging in the sand. He's waving for you to join him! You get to lie on the shore with Han!! Hints Imagine lying on the shore with Han Solo. Enjoying a cool drink. Smelling the fragrance of the rice paddy behind you. Yeah, this is the life!

meaningMnemonic: The leader squid tells all of its squid people to be thrifty . Hints Imagine the leader squid giving a speech about how you shouldn't buy new things, and how you should live with a roommate to save money. Every squid yen counts!
readingMnemonic: Who is a thrifty squid? Ken ( けん ) the samurai's squid buddy, who gets carried around in a bucket and never pays rent. Hints Ken's squid is always shaking his head at Ken the samurai's obsession with wearing all silk. He should visit Thrifty Threads, the second hand shop, and get some cotton clothes that would do the job just fine. Hint: Whenever there's a squid, remember that Ken ( けん ) the samurai is nearby.

meaningMnemonic: You put your fingers in the coffin to tickle the beggar inside. What you're doing is a new form of torture . Hints First, you put them in a coffin to make them think they're going to die. Then you tickle them with your fingers. There is no greater psychological + physical torture than this.
readingMnemonic: The beggar you will coffin tickle torture is none other than old Grandpa ごう いち . He is a frail old man, and doesn't like to be tickled. Hints He keeps screaming: "STOP THIS TICKLE TORTURE. I CAN'T TAKE IT, JUST BURY ME."

meaningMnemonic: Give alcohol to a demon and you'll see how ugly it really is. Demons need to concentrate to keep their disguises going. Even if it looked pretty when you met it, like super handsome, give it a few drinks and its facade will slide off and reveal its super gross demon face. Hints Picture the drunk demon as its pretty face drips off revealing the ugly crap piled underneath.
readingMnemonic: The ugly demon is drunk and taking off his shoe s ( しゅう ) and swinging them around his head. And, oh no, he's drinking more alcohol out of the shoes. Hints The demon drinking alcohol out of its nasty shoes is the ugliest scene you've ever seen.

meaningMnemonic: You go outside to bask your forehead in the sun , but then you see these creatures with lid s for heads and fins for feet. Uh… where did they come from? From the underworld . Nothing like them exists in this world. They obviously came from the underworld. Hints Imagine the heat of the sun on your forehead as you watch these horrible creatures with lid-heads and fin-feet. There's no doubt they're from the underworld, probably here to enjoy the sun. You might want to get out of their way…
readingMnemonic: These underworld creatures must be out and about because it's May ( めい ), and the weather is so fantastic and sunny right now. They don't get to see the sun down there in the underworld, so every May they turn up in droves to experience it. Hints Yes, even underworld creatures love to frolic around in the beautiful May weather.

meaningMnemonic: The tsunami swept away one of the cleat s your husband just bought and creates an entire valley with it. Hints Watch as the tsunami rakes your husband's cleat across the mountain, carving a valley and an easier path for itself. Nature is brutal.
readingMnemonic: When the water clears, you and your husband go to the valley to look for the cleat and instead you find a bunch of ca ke ( けい )! Maybe this is the tsunami's way of saying, "Thanks for letting me steal your cleat so I could make this valley shortcut." Hints Imagine yourself eating cake with your husband in this newly formed valley. You both agree that this should be called Cake Valley!

meaningMnemonic: Under your own roof , a geoduck jumps out of the ground with a sword and stabs your husband/wife/marriage partner to death. Now you're a widow . Hints Imagine the geoduck laughing and screaming, "Now you're a widow! Now you're a widow!" flailing the sword around. It's awful.
readingMnemonic: You may be a widow , but that doesn't make you weak. You run outside, jump into your ca r ( か ), and run your entire house and the geoduck over. Hints It's just you and your car now, living the widow life, driving on into the sunset and forgetting your past.

meaningMnemonic: You're walking in a greenhouse when you see a small drop of water fall and it makes you yearn for the person you adore . You haven't seen them in so long. But something about being in this greenhouse and seeing that tiny water droplet made your heart burst with longing. Hints Imagine how it feels to yearn for someone else when you see the small water drop. Imagine how your heart feels.
readingMnemonic: As you yearn for that person from your past, you look back at the drop and see... Bo bo ( ぼ ) the clown?! Ugh. Apparently Bobo dropped that small drop of water. Hints Now you yearn for being somewhere Bobo is not.

meaningMnemonic: A certain country is a certain country !
readingMnemonic: This word uses the on'yomi for both kanji, and you learned those readings with the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 日本に留学生を多く送りこんでいる某国で教えています。
sentences.english: I teach in a country that sends a lot of exchange students to Japan.

sentences.japanese: 梓川さんは派遣員として某国大使館に勤めていました。
sentences.english: Azusagawa-san worked as a temporary employee at a certain country's embassy.

sentences.japanese: 菅原沙羅が某国のスパイであるという嫌疑はぬぐえません。
sentences.english: We can't shake the suspicion that Sara Sugawara is a spy for a certain country.

meaningMnemonic: A certain family name belongs to a certain person .
readingMnemonic: This word uses the on'yomi for both kanji, and you learned those readings with the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 審査員の某氏に会いました。
sentences.english: I met with one of the judges.

sentences.japanese: 社長に近い立場の某氏は、「難しい状況にしてしまった」とコメントしている。
sentences.english: A certain person close to the president commented, "We've put ourselves in a difficult situation".

sentences.japanese: 「こういちはいつか世界を征服する」と某氏が語っていた。
sentences.english: A certain person told me that Koichi is going to conquer the world one day.

meaningMnemonic: No surprises here. A certain place is a certain place .
readingMnemonic: This word uses the on'yomi for both kanji, and you learned those readings with the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 栃木県の某所で行われたイベントに行ってきました。
sentences.english: I went to an event held at a certain place in Tochigi Prefecture.

sentences.japanese: 昨夜、某所にて、有名人による太鼓の演奏会が行われたようです。
sentences.english: Last night, there was a taiko performance by a celebrity at a certain place.

sentences.japanese: 彼女と出会ったのは、都内某所の居酒屋で食事をしている時だった。
sentences.english: I was eating at an izakaya in a certain place in Tokyo when I met my girlfriend.

meaningMnemonic: An article you write a promise on is an agreement . Make sure you read them thoroughly before you sign them!
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: きちんと約款を読みましたか？
sentences.english: Did you read the agreement thoroughly?

meaningMnemonic: Remember how you learned that 解剖 means "autopsy?" Well you have to learn about anatomy before you're going to be allowed to perform an autopsy or dissect anything.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 大学では解剖学を研究しています。
sentences.english: I study anatomy in college.

meaningMnemonic: Hide your name for anonymity . There's lots of that here on the internet. In fact, you're probably using a pseudonym right now, aren't you? Yeah, you are. You can't hide THAT from me at least... uh... Ssssteve?
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 匿名で投書をしました。
sentences.english: I wrote a letter to the editor anonymously.

meaningMnemonic: Article s that determine the rules and regulations of your job or a company are called articles of incorporation .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: この雛形を作れば簡単に定款が作成できます。
sentences.english: If I make this sample I can easily draw up a company statute.

meaningMnemonic: Barbarian s go around and commit acts of barbarism ! What else would they do? They're barbarians!
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: あいつらはそこで蛮行を繰り返しているんだ。
sentences.english: They repeated the brutality over there.

meaningMnemonic: Tap your head against the floor to show your subservient respect by doing this deep bow . This is the most respectful bow you can possibly do. 叩頭 refers to the traditional Chinese custom where individuals kneel and touch their foreheads to the ground as a gesture of deep respect or submission. You may come across the word 叩頭 in literature and drama set in historical China, particularly in imperial settings.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 叩 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Who's that bow ing before you? It's none other than こう いち ! He's bowing out of deep respect for you finally hitting level 60 on WaniKani. Congrats!

sentences.japanese: 叩頭とは、いわゆる日本の土下座のことです。
sentences.english: "Kowtow" is what is called "dogeza" in Japan.

sentences.japanese: 部屋の中にいた全員が、王に向かって叩頭した。
sentences.english: Everyone in the room got to their knees and bowed to the king, pressing their foreheads on the floor.

sentences.japanese: 中国の時代劇を見ている日本人以外は、「叩頭」という言葉はほとんど知らないかもしれませんね。
sentences.english: Apart from Japanese people watching Chinese historical dramas, most Japanese people may not be familiar with the term "kowtow."

meaningMnemonic: A groom gets a flower on his lapel and he's finally a real bridegroom ! Before that he was just waiting to be one. The flower makes it for real.
readingMnemonic: The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You learned them when you learned the kanji, so you should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 花婿が結婚式場から逃げ出したらしいわよ。
sentences.english: The groom ran away from the wedding!

meaningMnemonic: If you annoy someone who's busy they're still going to be busy . You annoying them can't change them. Though now they're probably busy AND annoyed.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 日々の煩忙から逃れ、ハワイにやって来ました。
sentences.english: I escaped from my busy daily life and came to Hawaii.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well.
readingMnemonic: This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

sentences.japanese: 某私立高校に伝わる、奇妙な噂があるんだ。
sentences.english: A strange rumor is circulating at a certain private high school.

sentences.japanese: 優秀な人は成長できる場に行きたがるんで、「高い目標」を目指している企業には、良い人材が多いんです。逆に言うと、良い人が集まらない企業は、目標が低いんですよ…某社のように、ね。
sentences.english: Talented people seek environments where they can grow, so companies that strive for "lofty goals" have a lot of great employees. Conversely, companies that don't attract good staff have unambitious goals… like a certain company we all know.

meaningMnemonic: This is a combination of the words 吸う meaning "to smoke" and 殻 meaning "shell" or "husk." The husk left over after you're done smoking is the cigarette butt . Or tobacco ashes if you just have a pile of them.
readingMnemonic: This is a combination of the words 吸う and 殻 . Change the う to い and don't forget the rendaku, and you should be able to remember this reading too!

meaningMnemonic: A manor with a park is still a manor — it's just a really big and impressive one. 庄園 refers to a medieval-style manor — a large agricultural estate granted to a lord by the monarch to be managed privately as a source of personal income. Many famous samurai families took their names from 庄園 , as they often managed them locally in place of absentee owners who preferred to hang out in Kyoto.

meaningMnemonic: The underworld dirt is another word for the realm of the dead , underworld , or Hades . Like the word 冥界 (also in this level), it's rather poetic, and mostly used in written contexts involving spirituality, Buddhism, and ancient mythologies. There are a few set expressions that only use 冥土 , though. One example is 冥土の土産 , "a souvenir to take to the realm of the dead". It refers to something abstract that is so valuable, it's worth taking to the underworld, such as the solution to a great mystery, or a happy memory. Another expression is 冥土の旅支度 , which means "preparations for the journey to the realm of the dead", and can refer to the preparation of the deceased before a funeral, as wells as certain preparations made by Buddhists while they're still alive. You'll also see this word written as 冥途 sometimes.

readingMnemonic: The reading can be either the on'yomi or kun'yomi, and you know both. Between the two, the on'yomi はんせん is the standard reading. As is often the case with on'yomi compounds, it has a more technical feel, so it is commonly used in formal references to sailing ships either in technical books or fiction. The kun'yomi ほぶね , on the other hand, has a softer, more traditionally Japanese tone, like how people in the past might have referred to it in everyday life. You'll often see it in older songs or literature, but it can also appear in modern works to convey a nostalgic vibe.

meaningMnemonic: From the south come the barbarians known as… the southern barbarians . They were the barbarians in the south, after all. Today this word mostly refers to nanban -style food named after those traders. (Think fried food and tartar sauce… Yum.)

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means yearn for , so the verb version is to yearn for . But that sounds kinda old fashioned, so you can just use to adore too.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You realize you're starting to yearn for someone way more than you used to. " Sh*t ( した )... " you say to yourself.
